author: Agence France-Presse
description:
Bank says gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily and the move will allow it to respond more rapidly in a ‘crisis situation’

The Dutch central bank says it has moved 86 tonnes of its gold reserves out of the US and Canada to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest”.

De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) said gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily than those held in New York and Ottawa.

Continue reading...
title: Dutch central bank moves 86 tonnes of gold to UK from US and Canada, citing ‘geopolitical unrest’

author: Jonathan Watts
description:
Oil consumption plummets and EV sales soar as analysts say demand may not fully return even if crude price falls

China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, thanks to a sharp reduction in oil consumption and a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles and public transport, analysis shows.

The report reveals the role of clean energy in cushioning the price shocks caused by the strait of Hormuz crisis to the world’s biggest oil importer. It also reinforces hopes that China, which is the world’s biggest greenhouse gas emitter, may be nearing a turning point in decarbonising its economy.

Continue reading...
title: China’s falling emissions amid Iran war spark hope of decarbonisation watershed

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency
description:
The city’s police department warns the public to stay away from the Minneapolis convention center

At least one person was killed and six others were injured in a shooting in downtown Minneapolis on Wednesday afternoon, officials said.

According to county spokesperson Joshua Yetman, the Hennepin county medical center received seven patients, one of them deceased. The identity of the deceased person was not released.

Continue reading...
title: One dead and multiple injured at shooting in downtown Minneapolis

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Black called on to comply with subpoenas and appear as required to clarify connections to convicted sex offender

More than a dozen survivors of Jeffrey Epstein’s abuse have called on the billionaire Leon Black to appear before the House oversight committee in order to clarify his connections to the late disgraced financier and convicted sex offender.

In a letter released on Wednesday, the survivors urged Black to comply with congressional subpoenas ahead of Thursday’s deposition before the House oversight committee.

Continue reading...
title: Epstein survivors urge billionaire Leon Black to cooperate with House panel

author: Associated Press
description:
Mississippi-born Wilson, who worked across folk, pop, R&B and country, was once dubbed America’s best singer

Cassandra Wilson, the two-time Grammy-winning jazz singer, songwriter and producer has died. She was 70.

Dubbed America’s best singer by Time magazine in 2001, Wilson was best known for her genre-bending voice, which expanded the boundaries of traditional blues-based jazz and worked effortlessly across folk, pop, R&B, country and beyond. At the heart of all her work was her idiosyncratic contralto, a soulful sound distinctly tied to her roots.

Continue reading...
title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-winning jazz singer, dies aged 70

author: Kiran StaceyPolicy editor
description:
PM will aim to centre talks with French president on key foreign policy issues such as Iran, smuggling gangs and EU relations

Andy Burnham will begin the process of courting European leaders when he welcomes Emmanuel Macron as the first foreign head of state to visit him in Downing Street.

The prime minister will meet the French president at No 10 on Thursday as he looks to make inroads on a number of foreign policy objectives, including curbing irregular migration and sealing a new deal with the EU.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham targets migrant crisis ahead of Macron’s visit to No 10

author: Guardian staff
description:
Treasurer says he acknowledges concerns about inflation, cost of living and real wages were on voters’ minds. Follow the day’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia will deploy a team of specialist drone operators to help the search and rescue effort in the deadly Nepal-Tibet floods.

Operators, including those from Fire and Rescue New South Wales and the Queensland fire department, will head to the disaster-struck region in the coming days.

While we await the committee’s final report, we are not waiting to act.

This investment will strengthen the important work of Call It Out and support efforts to collate rigorous data.
title: Australia news live: Jim Chalmers weighs in on One Nation WA byelection win; $2m for Indigenous racism online register

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Team circumvented salary cap rules to sign star

  • Owner Steve Ballmer lands one-year ban

The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Los Angeles Clippers after finding that the franchise circumvented salary cap rules when it courted Kawhi Leonard as a free agent.

The league has stripped the team of five first-round draft picks, giving the team no natural pick in the draft from 2029 through 2033.

Continue reading...
title: Clippers docked five first-round draft picks and fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandal

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
President’s order strips nearly 3m acres of Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante, sacred tribal sites, of safeguards

Patagonia, the outdoor clothing and gear company, has joined a lawsuit challenging Donald Trump’s decision to significantly reduce the Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments in Utah, removing protections from nearly 3m acres.

In July, the president approved the reduction of the sites by 90%, clearing the way to open the land to oil and gas companies. He argued in his proclamations that doing so would allow lands to be “put to a higher-priority use” and that the they contained critical minerals important to “ resource independence …[and] national security.”

Continue reading...
title: Patagonia sues Trump over reducing protected areas of Utah national monuments

author: Maya Yang
description:
Vice-president says on evangelical podcast he would feel ‘not shocked if the antichrist was walking among us’

JD Vance has said he is “doing as much of God’s work as possible” and that he is OK “if that leads to the end times”, which he says “are coming”.

The US vice-president made the comments during a Monday podcast interview with Bryce Crawford, a 22-year old evangelical host with over a million YouTube followers and videos featuring sensationalist headlines including “Preaching the gospel in Chicago’s deadliest neighborhood” and “Debating a ‘gay’ pastor”.

Continue reading...
title: JD Vance says he’s doing ‘God’s work – and if that leads to the end times, OK’

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Senatobia, where white officer shot and killed Kohen Wiley, terminates chief who reportedly used racist slurs in texts

Late Tuesday, the city of Senatobia, Mississippi fired its police chief, Harold Vanderford, after it was reported that Vanderford regularly used racist slurs against Black people in his text messages. The town, which is about 40% Black, made national news earlier this year after a white officer fatally shot and killed Kohen Wiley, a one-year-old Black baby, while responding to a shoplifting call at Walmart. Officers fired into a vehicle, shooting the driver and killing the toddler, who was being held in his mother’s arms.

Though Vanderford submitted a re
title: Police chief in Mississippi town where 1-year-old was killed has been fired

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Tech company submits to controversial Trump order to rename body of water amid US trade spat with Canada

Apple has renamed Lake Ontario to “Lake America” for US users of its Maps app, after an executive order from Donald Trump to change the name of the Great Lake amid his trade spat with Canada.

The Apple Maps app now displays the controversial new name for the lake, which sits between the border of New York state and the Canadian province of Ontario, for users in the US. Apple users outside the country will still see the Lake Ontario name.

Continue reading...
title: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ for US users after Trump order

author: Patrick Daly
description:
British tourists reportedly discovered Luger pistol that is latest in long line of potential leads in mystery of al-Hilli deaths

Experts are examining a gun found by tourists to determine whether it might have been used to kill a British family in the French Alps 14 years ago.

In what remains an unsolved murder case, Saad al-Hilli, 50, his wife, Ikbal, 47, and her mother, Suhaila al-Allaf, 74, were shot dead on a road near Annecy, a remote Alpine village in eastern France in September 2012.

Continue reading...
title: Gun found in French lake is analysed by 2012 Alps killings investigators

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Jury sent back for more deliberations in case of mother accused of murdering her three children

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial on Wednesday told the judge for a second time that it can’t agree on a verdict in the controversial case of the mother accused of murdering her three children.

The jury were then sent back for more deliberations but if they remain deadlocked for a third time a mistrial is set to be called in the high-profile case.

Continue reading...
title: Lindsay Clancy jurors say they’re deadlocked for a second time

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Monarch tells Emmanuel Macron at the British Museum in London that the two nations will share a future ‘woven together’ by history and shared values

The loan of the Bayeux tapestry was the “the best possible symbol” of the “entente amicale” between France and the UK, King Charles said as he visited the famous embroidered masterpiece at the British Museum in London.

Though the tapestry recounts a conflict, “here it is today, nearly 1,000 years later, as a precious symbol of trust, at a time when trust seems sadly to be in short supply between nations,” he said.

Continue reading...
title: Bayeux tapestry loan symbolises ‘entente amicale’ between France and UK, says King Charles

author: Andrew Roth Global affairs correspondent
description:
Defence minister says he believes US backing could tip regional balance in favour of forced resettlement

Israel’s defence minister has said his country is seeking Donald Trump’s support to approve plans to expel Palestinians from the Gaza Strip in what has widely been condemned as a potential war crime.

Israel Katz said there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this
migration” during a conference hosted by the Israeli news site Ynet and the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth. He said the Israeli government was “organised and prepared to get them out by sea, by air, by every way possible”.

Continue reading...
title: Israel ‘seeking Trump’s support for plan to expel Palestinians from Gaza’

author: Sam Levine in New York
description:
Experts have expressed deep concerns that the practice runs afoul of the fourth amendment’s right to privacy

Federal prosecutors have declined to say whether they secretly obtained phone records for the journalist Don Lemon using an unusual administrative summons, his lawyers said in a Monday court filing, highlighting concern about a controversial legal authority the government has claimed to gather information as it charged Lemon and dozens of others with civil rights crimes in connection to a January protest at a church in Saint Paul, Minnesota.

In January, officials served Verizon with an administrative summons for a log of Lem
title: US prosecutors refuse to say if they secretly obtained Don Lemon’s phone records

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Party leader in England and Wales seen as favourite to contest Holborn and St Pancras after Starmer’s resignation

Zack Polanski moved a step closer in his quest to become an MP on Wednesday, with local Green party members supporting him to become the party’s candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection.

The party leader in England and Wales started campaigning alongside his fellow Green, Hannah Spencer, the MP for Gorton and Denton, in the Holborn area on Tuesday, and is seriously considering putting himself forward as the party’s candidate in the seat vacated by Keir Starmer on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Green party members back Zack Polanski to stand in London byelection

author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
description:
Over 40% of films in LFF programme are female-made, but only two of 21 gala films are directed by women

Female film-makers are still being squeezed out of the industry as they progress beyond their debut films, the director of the London film festival has said, adding that “the dial does not seem to be moving”.

Kristy Matheson’s comments came as LFF announced its full programme for this year’s event, which runs from 7 to 19 October. Of the 251 titles, 109 (43%) are made by female film-makers, but only two of the 21 gala films are directed by women.

Continue reading...
title: Female film-makers still being squeezed out of industry, London film festival director says

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Paul Miller, an openly racist fighter, derided Ben Azoulay, and a spectator was ejected for waving a swastika flag

Democrats in Florida have condemned a professional mixed martial arts event in Orlando at which an openly racist fighter derided his beaten opponent as “a short little fucking Jew prick”, and a spectator was ejected for waving a giant swastika flag.

Anna Eskamani, a Democratic state representative running to become the city’s mayor, said Saturday’s event, and the assertion by city officials that they were compelled to host it, were unacceptable.

Continue reading...
title: MMA fight in Florida condemned after fighter’s antisemitic comments

author: Nils Pratley
description:
Fair to say the current sell-off is international, but the PM has said little yet to make investors rethink the UK’s status

It’s too soon to say the bond markets have turned on Andy Burnham. Tuesday’s spike in gilt yields, taking the UK’s 30-year borrowing costs to their highest level since 1998, was part of an international sell-off of government debt.

The main contributors are well known. The Iran war, by increasing the cost of energy, has overturned the comforting start-of-the-year thesis of falling global inflation and interest rates. A plunging Japanese yen has kicked away another assumed source of financial stability. The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, hasn’t calmed nerves with his solo, and so far futile,
title: Burnham beware, the bond markets will demand proper answers in the budget | Nils Pratley

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
The government’s increasingly hostile stance towards the Kremlin has drawn criticism from the far right – and the far left

Even before the German government laid the blame this week on Russia for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport, the topic of German ties to Moscow was high on the political agenda.

But the timing of the unsurprising yet explosive Leipzig announcement – days before a key regional vote – has exposed the extent to which German politics is polarised on the issue.

Continue reading...
title: Leipzig airport attack fallout lays bare Germany’s polarisation on Russia

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
Various laws and 250 years of tradition prevent the likeness of living people from appearing on currency. Donald Trump and Scott Bessent don’t want you to worry about that

  • This was originally published in This Week in Trumpland. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday

Two hallmarks of Donald Trump’s second-term: the president’s enthusiasm for putting his name and face on things, and his cavalier approach to established law.

Today the president is once again combining both those interests, as the government releases a $1 coin bearing his image, an item of currency which scholars say should be illegal, but which is happening anyway. How many times have you heard that in the last 18 months?

Continue reading...
title: The $1 Trump coin: legal tender, depending on what you mean by legal

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
While leaders focused on Hasan Piker, two of the party’s more conservative members salvaged a GOP measure that was poised to fail

House Democratic leaders have spent the past few weeks waging a bitter campaign against their own left flank over a leftwing streamer. On Tuesday, it was the party’s center-right who blindsided them.

Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, announced late on Tuesday that he had asked the Democratic caucus’s committee on caucus rules to consider punishing the retiring Jared Golden of Maine and Blue Dog Coalition leader Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington after the pair sided with Republicans on a procedural vote that had appeared doomed.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic party infighting engulfs center-right over House rules vote

author: Philip Oltermann in Venice
description:
Actor says the press baron’s daughter Elisabeth told him her father was pleased, ‘but he hadn’t seen the film at that point’

Rupert Murdoch is “very happy” that he’s being portrayed by Guy Pearce in a new film about the origins of British tabloid the Sun, the Australian actor has said.

Speaking at the Venice film festival ahead of the premiere of 28 Days Later director Danny Boyle’s Ink, Pearce said he had been messaging with the media tycoon’s daughter Elisabeth “and she did say ‘Dad’s very happy that you’re playing him’.”

Continue reading...
title: Rupert Murdoch ‘very happy’ that Guy Pearce plays him in Fleet Street biopic Ink

author: Helena Horton
description:
Guardian city editor Anna Isaac, investigative reporter Peter Geoghegan and broadcaster Michael Crick refused entry

Reform UK has banned at least three journalists who have investigated the party and Nigel Farage from its annual conference, which begins on Thursday.

The Guardian’s City editor, Anna Isaac, the investigative reporter Peter Geoghegan and the broadcaster and biographer Michael Crick were told this week that their credentials to cover the event had been declined.

Continue reading...
title: Reform UK bans three journalists who have investigated party from its conference

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Landmark lawsuit claims tech company’s pay-setting system has breached privacy laws and pushed down earnings

Uber drivers have launched a landmark legal action against the ride-hailing company claiming they live in “constant fear” of a “soulless” algorithm it uses to set pay and allocate jobs.

Drivers from the UK, the Netherlands and other countries have joined the compensation claim that could run into billions of dollars. It alleges an AI-powered pay-setting system breaches data protection laws and pushes down their earnings.

Continue reading...
title: Uber drivers launch European class action over ‘soulless’ and ‘scary’ AI algorithm

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform UK leader dismisses criticism of his failure to register £5m gift as a sign of a ‘complainants’ society’

Nigel Farage has compared his situation to that of Donald Trump being pursued by investigators for years, saying both of them are “outsiders” up against “the system”, as he admitted having become tetchy and aggrieved this summer.

The Reform UK leader has been under huge scrutiny over his finances after failing to declare a £5m gift from the Thailand-based donor Christopher Harborne and further financial support from a friend, the fraudster George Cottrell, before the last election.

Continue re
title: Farage compares standards inquiry to investigations faced by fellow ‘outsider’ Trump

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Teachers and parents have warned against AI use in schools over concerns of ‘cognitive surrender’

New York City will ban students’ use of artificial intelligence in public schools through eighth grade, typically age 13 or 14. The prohibition is scheduled to be announced on Wednesday and will go into effect next week.

The change is part of a sweeping overhaul of the use of technology in the US’s largest school district, which enrolls roughly 900,000 students a year. In another policy shift, classrooms will keep students off laptops or tablets through the third grade, age nine or 10. The city’s public school technology policies are closely watched by the rest of the United States.

Continue reading...
title: New York City to ban student AI use in public schools until high school

author: Associated Press
description:
Top medical groups band together to ease confusion from Trump administration’s changing immunization advice

Leading US medical groups are urging people to get updated flu and Covid-19 vaccinations this fall, banding together Wednesday to issue shot guidelines – and highlight the science behind them – saying they hope to ease confusion caused by the Trump administration’s changing advice.

Flu vaccinations are beginning and the latest coronavirus shots are starting to arrive after the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved this year’s updated versions last week. Winter also brings another vaccine-preventable risk called RSV.

Continue reading...
title: US medical groups urge people to get flu and Covid shots in counter to Trump guidance

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Exclusive: Eyad Shadid launches civil case in district court after charges against him dropped, alleging he was ‘battered’ near Sydney’s town hall in February

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Palestinian Australian man who alleges he was punched in the face when trying to stop police from harassing Muslim men praying during an anti–Isaac Herzog protest is suing New South Wales over “a series of false accusations”.

Eyad Shadid has launched a civil case in the NSW district court, alleging he was assaulted, battered and falsely imprisoned by police near Sydney’s town hall.
title: Palestinian Australian sues NSW police claiming he was punched at Herzog rally when helping prayer group

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
ABS’s snapshot of Australia’s accounts shows economic growth – albeit low – in the face ‘challenging international circumstances’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian Bureau of Statistics released its latest set of national accounts, which give us a snapshot of how the economy is performing in the quarter, and what’s happening under the hood.

Here are the three things you need to know.

Continue reading...
title: We’re purchasing EVs instead of holidaying in Europe – and what else we learned from Australia’s national accounts

author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Energy secretary Chris Wright denies US seeks to ‘take’ country’s oil, saying deal is ‘transformation’ of relations

The US energy secretary, Chris Wright, has denied Washington is seeking to commandeer huge quantities of Venezuelan oil, amid growing criticism of Donald Trump’s energy deal with the country’s interim leaders.

“Absolutely not,” Wright replied when asked by a CNBC journalist if the US was engaged in a “heavy-handed” attempt to “take” Venezuelan oil in violation of the South American country’s constitution.

Continue reading...
title: Trump ally defends Venezuela oil deal amid ‘gunpoint diplomacy’ criticism

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
US defense secretary faced backlash for attempting to mock Canada’s armed forces amid trade war

A social media post by Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of defense, body-shaming female members of a Canadian youth development program remained online on Wednesday despite a furious backlash on both sides of the border.

On Monday night Hegseth posted on X a photograph of two people in uniform with a Canadian flag and the caption “this is real”, an apparent attempt at mocking the country’s armed forces amid the Trump administration’s trade spat with its northern neighbor.

Continue reading...
title: Pete Hegseth criticized for body-shaming Canadian cadet program members

author: Luke Harding
description:
Whether or not US president fits the definition of a Russian asset, his actions align closely with the Kremlin’s interests

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Could Donald Trump be a Russian asset? The headline on a review in the Guardian of my new book Betrayal has provoked heated international debate. Written by the historian Lawrence Freedman, the piece generated thousands of comments from across Europe and beyond on social media. Many people responded with a single word: “Duh!”

Trump’s relationship with Vladimir Putin is the biggest
title: What’s really behind Trump’s deference to Putin?

author: Helena Horton
description:
Campaigners say pheasants and partridges reared ‘on industrial scale’ do not have same protections as chickens

The government is considering a crackdown on pheasant shooting in England as part of a consultation on strict new animal welfare laws that would affect shoot organisers.

Ministers are already considering plans for the issuing of licences for those who run game bird shoots. The proposals mean anybody associated with wildlife crime, such as the poisoning or shooting of birds of prey, would be banned from hosting shooting events.

Continue reading...
title: Mass breeding of game birds without welfare checks may be curtailed in England

author: Adria R Walker
description:
New law requires cosmetology classes to give instruction on all hair types from the kinkiest to the straightest

As of 1 September, a new law in New York state requires hairdressers studying cosmetology to be trained to work with all hair types.

“This is about equal access to service,” assembly member Michaelle Solages, who sponsored the law, said in a statement earlier this year. “No New Yorker should ever walk into a salon and be turned away or receive substandard care because of their hair texture. Now, with the adoption of this legislation, they won’t have to.”

Continue reading...
title: New York law requires hairdressers to learn how to work with all hair types

author: Ben Doherty
description:
As a major new biography of the former prime minister goes on sale, he talks about meeting the Queen, Trump’s aims, and why his big vision will never fade

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queen Elizabeth II met Paul Keating “alone, to her credit” in what the prime minister was informed was her great-great-grandmother, Queen Victoria’s, favourite room at Balmoral Castle.

“And I took some pleasure in explaining the furniture to her,” Keating recalls, an old elan breaking through.
title: ‘Timidity is a virus’: Paul Keating fights the fading of the light as he seeks to enshrine his legacy

author: Dara Kerr
description:
The company says it prioritizes safety, but suits allege its ChatGPT bot induced shooter to carry out attack in Canada

OpenAI faces 30 new lawsuits filed on behalf of victims of the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.

The suits, filed on Wednesday, allege the company’s ChatGPT chatbot induced the shooter to carry out the attack in rural Canada in February, in which eight people were killed and dozens more wounded – most of them children.

Continue reading...
title: Tumbler Ridge mass shooting victims file 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
Minister says Sweden has ‘fulfilled its commitments’ amid criticism of ‘unjust’ decisions such as case of Joyce Thomas

The Swedish government has doubled down on its position on removing and deporting British citizens on the grounds they were late to apply for permission to stay after Brexit.

The migration minister, Johan Forssell, issued a robust defence of the Swedish migration agency’s implementation of the Brexit withdrawal agreement on Wednesday in response to a question from an MP about the case of Joyce Thomas, a 78-year-old British widow who has been ordered to leave the country after 21 years.
title: Swedish minister defends strict post-Brexit removals of Britons

author: Guardian staff
description:
Woman from Reno was swimming near Hidden beach when river otter attacked her, Tahoe’s second incident in a month

A swimmer at Lake Tahoe in Nevada was bitten by a river otter in an incident that left her needing to go to hospital and get 38 stitches for her wounds as well as rabies shots, local media have reported.

Lynnette Bellin from Reno was swimming near Hidden beach on the Nevada side of the popular tourist attraction on Sunday when she was attacked by the creature.

Continue reading...
title: US woman gets 38 stitches after being bitten by otter in Lake Tahoe

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
In first PMQs clash with Kemi Badenoch, prime minister rejects comparison to Liz Truss’s government

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham blamed the Conservatives’ legacy for leaving the UK vulnerable to market turmoil, in his first prime ministers’ questions clash with Kemi Badenoch, as the UK’s borrowing costs climbed further.

The Conservative leader compared the market pressure on Burnham’s second day to Liz Truss’s mini-Budget. But the prime minister said it was the Tories’ failure to address the UK’s growth and debt which meant the economy was exposed to market shocks.

Continue r
title: Andy Burnham blames Tory legacy for leaving UK economy vulnerable

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Pay and shares deal nearly matches $58m award to John Ternus, his successor as CEO at the $4.7tn tech company

  • Business live – latest updates

Tim Cook has received a $47m (£35m) pay deal as Apple’s executive chair, a remuneration package that nears the level set for his successor as chief executive.

Cook, who handed over to John Ternus on Tuesday, will be paid a base salary of $2m and $45m worth of shares. Half of the share award will be based on performance targets being met, while the remaining half will be paid out over four years.
title: Tim Cook handed $47m package for new role as executive chair of Apple

author: Reuters
description:
US energy department warns of potential for outages in PJM Interconnection, serving 67 million from DC to Chicago

The risk ⁠of power outages ⁠is expected to ​escalate across a broad swath of the United States on Wednesday as intense heat will test the capacity of electricity supplies ⁠serving millions of homes and businesses from the midwest through the mid-Atlantic.

The US Department of Energy warned of the potential for heightened blackout risks in ⁠the PJM Interconnection, the largest US electric grid, which serves 67 million people in ​a territory stretching from Washington DC to ‌Chicago.

Continue reading...
title: Blackout risk rises as heatwave stresses largest US electric grids

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Rapper’s supporters reflect on ‘astonishing’ events leading to Duane Davis being found guilty over 1996 fatal shooting

A criminal conviction this week in the murder of Tupac Shakur, the first since the rapper was gunned down in 1996, sent shockwaves through his sea of fans who have waited three decades for answers.

Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a former California gang leader, was found guilty of murder on Monday for the role he played in orchestrating the fatal shooting of Shakur.
title: ‘It always comes around’: fans react to conviction in Tupac Shakur’s murder 30 years later

author: William Christou in Beirut
description:
Blast also injures 68 guests at the wedding in southern Iran, prompting fears of escalation in hostilities

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

Iran has accused the US of a “war crime” after a missile blast killed at least five people and injured 68 who were attending a wedding at a private home in a coastal city of southern Iran, as the fresh exchange of strikes prompted fears of a wider renewal of hostilities.

Iranian media said that the wedding ceremony was being held in a home in the city of Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, late on Tuesday when a US missile struck, with shrapnel and debris from the strike killing and injuring people.
title: Iran accuses US of ‘war crime’ after missile blast kills five people at wedding

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Cao has been serving as acting navy secretary since John Phelan departed the job unexpectedly and without explanation in late April

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Two of the Democratic representatives who defected and joined the Republicans in voting in favor of a resolution condemning socialism and the Democratic Socialists of America organisation have defended their actions on social media.

Democratic leaders in the US House had sharply criticized the representatives for defecting and joining with Republicans in order to advance a procedural vote.

I just voted to fund government through December 11, preventing a shutdown in October. The bil
title: Trump nominates loyalist Hung Cao to be permanent navy secretary – US politics live

author: Achol Arok
description:
A man shot dead in Merrylands West was not known to police, in a case with similarities to Monday’s killing in Campbelltown

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales police are investigating the death of a man who was shot dead in a home in Sydney’s west as a potential case of mistaken identity, marking the second fatal shooting incident in as many days.

Emergency services responded to reports of a shooting at a property in Merrylands West at about 3.15pm, where a man believed to be in his 30s sustained a gunshot wound.

Continue reading...
title: Fatal Sydney shooting could be another case of mistaken identity, police say

author: Press Association
description:
The two men and two women are also accused of causing or allowing death of a child and perverting course of justice

Four people have been charged with murder after a newborn baby girl was stabbed to death in Sheffield.

Two men and two women are to appear in court on Wednesday accused of murder, causing or allowing the death of a child, and perverting the course of justice by taking steps to conceal the killing of an infant.

Continue reading...
title: Four charged with murder after newborn baby stabbed to death in Sheffield

author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv and Pjotr Sauer
description:
Ukrainian president says aviation industry needs to take account of growing number of Ukrainian attack drones in Russia

  • Europe live – latest updates

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Russia’s airspace is becoming unsafe for commercial airlines, as Vladimir Putin promised to step up strikes against Ukraine’s energy facilities in the run-up to winter.

The Ukrainian president said there was no intention to directly threaten civilian flights, but the growing number of Ukrainian attack drones flying into the country would have to be “taken into account” by the aviation industry.

Continue reading...
title: Russian airspace becoming unsafe for commercial airlines, Zelenskyy says

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site

Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.

Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.

Continue reading...
title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Relatives of Benjamin Halona remember his career as wildlife firefighter and his zeal for selling tamales

Relatives of a New Mexico man who was fatally mauled by a bear inside his home recently say they are choosing to remember his firefighting career and zeal for peddling tamales rather than his rare, brutal manner of death.

As Benjamin Halona’s sister, Gloria Halona, and her daughter, Samantha Vandever, put it, that is the least he deserved after the quiet dignity that he showed becoming a widower in February and subsequently grappling with health problems that required him to use a walker and a wheelchair to move around.

Continue reading...
title: Family pays tribute to New Mexico man killed by bear: ‘He was a strong person’

author: Rob Davies
description:
Fully electric SUV unveiled after year-long delay and will be built at Jaguar Land Rover’s plant in Solihull

Range Rover has launched its first electric vehicle – a year later than planned – offering a greener option for fans of gargantuan British-made SUVs who are also conscious about the climate crisis.

Due to be built in Solihull, the home of the marque since 1970, the vehicle comes with an eye-watering price tag, starting at £154,070.

Continue reading...
title: Range Rover launches its first electric vehicle, with starting price of £154,070

author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
description:
Book recreates recipes from period following end of Spanish civil war when people faced food shortages

Few dishes are simpler to prepare than Spain’s signature dish of tortilla de patatas, which – aside from disputes about onions – requires nothing more than two basic ingredients and a pinch of salt. But where to begin if you have neither eggs nor potatoes?

That is the question the chef and food writer Berta Álvarez Acal sets out to answer in Recetas de Guerra (Wartime Recipes), a compilation of recipes covering the years of hunger after the end of the Spanish civil war in 1939.

Continue reading...
title: No eggs, no potatoes but ‘a lot of imagination’: how Spain cooked in war’s hunger years

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Budget carrier says airlines could go bust as it cuts passenger targets to reduce exposure to ‘unhedged winter oil’

  • Business live – latest updates

Ryanair has warned that air fares in Europe will jump next year if the oil price remains high and that some airlines could go bust.

The Irish budget carrier has cut its passenger target for the year to 31 March, down from 216 million customers to 214 million, to help reduce its exposure to “unhedged winter oil” during the unprofitable off season, with jet fuel currently trading at $140 (£104) a barrel.

Continue reading...
title: Ryanair warns air fares in Europe will jump next year if oil price stays high

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
UK borrowing costs driven up, adding to challenges facing John Healey as he prepares for first budget

  • Business live – latest updates

The global government bond sell-off resumed on Wednesday, driving up the UK’s borrowing costs and exacerbating the challenges facing John Healey as he prepares his first budget.

The yield – effectively the interest rate – on 10-year UK government bonds, or gilts, jumped to just below 5.3% in early trading: its highest level since mid-2008.

Continue reading...
title: Global bond sell-off intensifies as US-Iran tensions stoke inflation fears

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
London mayor convicted under controversial system where magistrates can decide outcomes in seconds

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The London mayor, Sadiq Khan, has been convicted and fined for not taxing a 24-year-old car, through a controversial fast-track court system.

He was found guilty last month under a system critics have described as “conveyor-belt justice”, with magistrates deciding on hundreds of daily cases and sometimes spending less than a minute on them.

Continue reading...
title: Sadiq Khan fined by fast-track court over untaxed car City Hall says is not his

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Ian Tyler, who was already in role on interim basis, selected and pledges to ‘lead the board’s evolution’

BP has appointed a new chair after a months-long search following the controversial ousting of Albert Manifold, seeking to draw a line under the boardroom turmoil at the oil and gas company.

Ian Tyler, who has served as the interim chair and sat on the BP board as a non-executive director since April 2025, is assuming the role on a permanent basis immediately.

Continue reading...
title: BP appoints new chair after contentious ousting of Albert Manifold in May

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
PMQs comes as Resolution Foundation says it is not ‘realistic’ to think defence spending can increase without tax rises

Good morning. Andy Burnham will face PMQs for the first time as PM today but he already has a fairly good idea of the questions he might get from Kemi Badenoch because she rehearsed them all yesterday. Here is an excerpt from the press release the Conservatives put out yesterday summarising those questions – and their take on how Burnham responded.

Kemi Badenoch asked if Burnham would:

-Set out a plan to get defence spending to 3% of GDP;

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to face first PMQs as borrowing costs rise – UK politics live

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Foreign policy chief says drone attack last month ‘had all the hallmarks of state sponsored terrorism’ as she prepares to lead today’s discussions

Britain’s foreign secretary Ed Miliband is also taking part in today’s talks in Ireland.

“We see an attempt by Russia to divide us in Europe and to deter us from our support for Ukraine. And I say very clearly today, on behalf of the United Kingdom, this attempt will fail.”

Continue reading...
title: EU holds talks on response to Leipzig drone attack after Germany formally blames Moscow for incident – Europe live

author: Ben Quinn
description:
Consumer watchdog Which? set up and accepted payment for fake listing for ‘1 bed apartment in heart of London’

Successive politicians have clawed their way past colleagues over the years to call the residence home. Yet in an offer that probably seemed too good to be true, the property site Booking.com has been accused of “systemic security failures” after it was able to set up and accept payment for a fake listing for 10 Downing Street.

A property listed as a “1 bedroom apartment in the heart of London” – with the exact address and a picture of the prime minister’s home – was listed on 18 June by researchers from the consumer watchdog Which?.

Continue reading...
title: Fake 10 Downing Street listing on Booking.com highlights security failures

author: Maya Goodfellow
description:
Arthur Downing, author of Power and the People: A History of British Energy, says all-encompassing rapid transition will need a mutualised system

Have you ever wondered why it is that most houses in the UK are reliant on gas boilers? Not what’s stopping more people from replacing them with heat pumps, but instead why and how the gas boiler became so ubiquitous in the first place?

Arthur Downing, the author of the new book Power and the People: A History of British Energy, can tell you exactly why. “We only have boilers in our houses because of a state-owned enterprise that went into everybody’s home and installed natural gas-suitable appliances at no direct cost,” he says. The nationalised gas industry of the 1940s to the 1980s, which oversaw this huge project, was for three decades one of the “most dynamic, innovative, efficient industries in Britain”, Downing says. Yet few of us would use t
title: Britain is OK with public ownership, but only by foreign powers. Why?

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Study reveals that pesticide poisoning kills 11,000 people each year, with India accounting for nearly 60% of fatalities

Almost half of the world’s farmers are poisoned by pesticides every single year, a study has found.

Using publicly available data from 2006-2023, the study, which was commissioned by Pesticide Action Network, found there to be an estimated 402-433m cases of unintentional acute pesticide poisoning of farmers and farm workers every year.

Continue reading...
title: Almost half of world’s farmers poisoned by pesticides every year, experts find

author: Philip Oltermann European culture editor
description:
Sergei Loznitsa likens removal of €2m grant to ‘a punishment in kindergarten’ on eve of Venice film festival

One of Ukraine’s most acclaimed film-makers has criticised the European Commission’s decision to cut off funds to the Venice Biennale over the opening of Russia’s pavilion, likening it to “a punishment in kindergarten”.

The Biennale drew heavy criticism this spring when it allowed Russia to use its pavilion for the first time since 2022, despite the ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Continue reading...
title: Ukrainian film-maker criticises EU after it cuts Venice Biennale funding over Russia controversy

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Exclusive: sanctions against ministers and settler groups are ‘smoke and mirrors cop-out’ says Omar Barghouti

Britain’s legal and ethical obligation to stop a genocide in Gaza requires it to take bigger steps than halting trade with illegal Israeli settlements or imposing further sanctions, Omar Barghouti, the co-founder of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement has said.

He described sanctions against individual settler groups or extremist ministers as a “smoke and mirrors cop-out and distraction” from the UK’s legal obligation under international law to end all support for Israel, including arms exports, trade deals and academic relations that “may directly or indirectly enable Israel’s illegal occupation” of Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem.

Continue reading...
title: UK must end all trade with Israel, says co-founder of BDS movement

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Police say the sheep were stolen from a property 830km west of Brisbane between February and May

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queensland police are investigating after about 5,500 Dorper sheep worth more than $1.7m were allegedly stolen from a western Queensland farm.

Police said the sheep were stolen from a property outside Blackall, about 830km west of Brisbane, between February and May this year.

Continue reading...
title: Queensland police investigate after 5,500 sheep worth $1.7m stolen from farm

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Hundreds of university staff were stationed at picket lines, calling for stronger protections around the use of AI

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The same week union members at the University of Sydney agreed to a 24-hour strike, staff received the results of an internal survey.

In the faculty of arts and social sciences, 0% agreed with the statement: “I trust the University of Sydney to act in the best interests of staff, students and the broader community.”
title: ‘We have had enough’: thousands of University of Sydney staff walk off the job over AI and job security

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: Communities from Scotland to India are pushing back against datacentres they feel have been forced upon them, warning they threaten energy supplies and the climate

Good morning. This summer, datacentres have become targets of resistance across the world. Ever since the arrival of ChatGPT, big tech has been lobbying for the creation of enormous new facilities. Many governments claim they’re essential in any country that wants to cash in on AI.

Campaigners argue datacentres drain resources and exacerbate the climate crisis. The Scottish National Party has backed a moratorium on new developments; so has the Greens. The boom has been immense, and so has the backlash. Today’s newsletter explains why.

UK politics | Andy Burnham has blamed Brexit and Margaret Thatcher
title: Wednesday briefing: ​What’s behind the global backlash against datacentres?

author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
description:
Speed limit dropped from 60km/h for around 70% of general roads in the hope of making narrow streets of crowded cities safer

Drivers on residential roads in Japan have been forced to take their foot off the accelerator, after the speed limit was slashed from 60km/h (37mph) to 30km/h in an attempt to reduce deaths and injuries among pedestrians on narrow urban streets.

The new limit, which went into effect on Tuesday, applies to residential roads with no centre line or maximum speed signs, media reports said.

Continue reading...
title: Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Lehrmann is accused of raping a woman in 2021 and will stand trial in Toowoomba in November. He intends to contest the charges

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jurors in the pending trial of Bruce Lehrmann for alleged rape could be questioned about their prior knowledge of him and the case.

Lehrmann, 31, is set to stand trial from 2 November, accused of twice raping a woman at a house in regional Queensland in 2021.

Continue reading...
title: Jury in Bruce Lehrmann’s Queensland rape trial may face questions about prior knowledge of case

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
John Sellers, 34, who moved with his family to Sweden aged 10, has been ejected despite his recent marriage to a Swede

A 34-year-old British man who has lived in Sweden since he was 10 has been deported in the latest of a series of Brexit-induced catastrophes for UK citizens in the country.

John Sellers was told to leave despite living in Sweden for 24 years, having been educated in the country and newly married to his Swedish partner, Caroline.

Continue reading...
title: British man deported from Sweden despite living there since childhood

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Hadley is giving evidence in trial of former 2GB rival Jones, 85, who has pleaded not guilty to 22 indecent assault and sexual touching charges

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

  • Warning: This article contains offensive language

Broadcaster Ray Hadley has told a Sydney court he used a homophobic slur and derogatory names when talking about his colleague Alan Jones, after 2GB withdrew a secret offer of a $4m contract to take over Jones’s coveted breakfast slot.

Hadley agreed under cross-examination by defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC that he told police in 2019 that Jones had recruited colleagues at 2GB to “dig up some dirt” on him.
title: Ray Hadley used homophobic slur against Alan Jones after 2GB withdrew offer of $4m breakfast radio gig, court hears

author: Reuters
description:
Decision marks a significant turning point in a case that sparked a national debate in Italy

A British-Australian couple will be allowed to spend more time with their three children after the ⁠youngsters were removed from the family’s off-grid woodland home in central Italy last year, their lawyer said on Tuesday.

The juvenile court ⁠of L’Aquila in Italy has ⁠approved a ​staged process under the supervision of social services that could ultimately allow the children to leave the residential care facility ⁠where they have been living since November.

Continue reading...
title: Off-grid UK-Australian couple given more access to children who were removed from home in Italy

author: Danny Vincent in Hong Kong
description:
Wong, 29, is accused of urging foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades and other hostile measures against China

Joshua Wong, one of Hong Kong’s most prominent pro-democracy activists, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to conspiring to seek foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China, a national security charge that carries a maximum life sentence.

Prosecutors have accused Wong, 29, of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China.

Continue reading...
title: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in second national security case

author: Adam Morton
description:
But scientists say the world could get back to 1.5C through deep, rapid emissions cuts and removing carbon from the atmosphere

Global heating will reach at least 1.8C under even the most optimistic future, well beyond the Paris agreement goal of 1.5C, according to a UN report that warns every fraction of temperature rise intensifies destructive extreme weather, glacier melt, ecosystem loss, and island and coastal city submersion.

The report by the Nairobi-based UN Environment Programme confirmed overshooting the 1.5C goal inscribed in the landmark Paris agreement of 2015 was now “unavoidable” and, despite some progress in addressing the human-caused climate crisis driven by burning fossil fuels, likely in the next few years.

Continue reading...
title: Global heating will hit at least 1.8C, UN warns, and there are ‘no good outcomes’

author: Natasha May in Pattaya, and agencies
description:
Ship has been plagued by reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health because of lengthy deployment

The USS Abraham Lincoln, an US aircraft carrier at the centre of a row over conditions on board after months at sea as part of Donald Trump’s war against Iran, has arrived off a Thai port.

Reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health on the vessel, including attempted suicides, have made headlines around the world, provoking criticism of the president’s actions in the Middle East.

Continue reading...
title: USS Abraham Lincoln arrives at Thai port after gruelling 270 days at sea

author: Chris Stein
description:
Incumbent, 80, beats back challenge from Seth Moulton, who argued Markey was too old to be effective at his job

Senator Ed Markey won the Democratic primary in Massachusetts on Tuesday, beating back a challenge from Seth Moulton, a congressman who tried to unseat him by arguing to voters his opponent was too old to be effective at his job.

Massachusetts is heavily Democratic, making the senator favored to win a third full term in the November general election, where he faces the Republican nominee John Deaton.

Continue reading...
title: Senator Ed Markey wins Massachusetts Democratic primary

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
In a major LGBTQ+ rights victory, the justice department cannot force the state to ban trans girls from women’s sports

A federal judge has dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit challenging California’s policy of allowing transgender youth to play on sports teams that match their gender, a major loss for Donald Trump and the Department of Justice (DoJ).

The justice department had been fighting for a year to force California to ban trans girls from women’s sports, with the president directly singling out one trans track and field athlete in online attacks and regularly mocking trans athletes in his speeches.

Continue reading...
title: Federal judge tosses Trump lawsuit over young trans athletes in California school sports

author: Associated Press
description:
Acting secretary picked for top role as critics accuse president of overworking sailors during war with Iran

Donald Trump said Tuesday that he is nominating acting navy secretary Hung Cao for the permanent job, giving the navy combat veteran the nod as concerns have emerged that some sailors have been stretched to the limit during the Iran war.

Cao has been serving as acting navy secretary since John Phelan departed the job unexpectedly and without explanation in late April.

Continue reading...
title: Trump nominates loyalist Hung Cao to be permanent navy secretary

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Government talks up pact but Venezuelan opposition alarmed that democracy yet to return after Maduro exit

Trump administration officials on Tuesday defended a highly contentious deal giving the US control of a significant chunk of Venezuelan oil reserves, arguing that the sweeping agreement would help stabilize and rebuild democracy in the shattered South American country while giving Washington vital access to strategic crude reserves.

Last week, Donald Trump announced a “groundbreaking” deal that would give the US “majority” control over 65bn barrels – roughly one-fifth – of Venezuela’s oil reserves.

Continue reading...
title: US officials defend Venezuela oil deal amid questions over rebuilding plan

author: Sarah Collard Indigenous affairs correspondent
description:
Other families have been unlawfully compelled to be case managed without consent, watchdog finds

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than a third of all reports raising concerns about the future welfare of unborn children were closed due to a shortage of allocated caseworkers, while families were unlawfully compelled to take part in prenatal case work, the New South Wales ombudsman has found.

In its findings after investig
title: More than a third of prenatal reports to NSW protective services not investigated, ombudsman finds
